favorite.name: Thomas Speer
favorite.case: Puka locked in the 9th, then ARSB, Hampton, and McBride. Best roster in the league, and he's chasing ring four.

board.name: Thomas Speer
board.case: Puka locked in the 9th, then ARSB, Hampton, and McBride. Best roster in the league, and he's chasing ring four.

board.name: Bryan Hunt
board.case: Chase at 3 and Bowers in the 9th. Finally a roster that matches the perennial-contender resume.

board.name: James Brochu
board.case: Lamb, Nico, Breece, and ETN kept in the 8th. Jigalos is back in the mix.

board.name: George Travis
board.case: CMC at 2, Kyren and Javonte behind him. The commissioner always drafts a team you have to game-plan.

board.name: Brian Heino
board.case: Achane in the 12th is the steal of the night, and Saquon fell to 11. The RBs are a title window.

board.name: Trevor Hash
board.case: Gibbs 1.01 and Chase Brown kept in the 9th. The RBs are elite — the rest has to catch up.

board.name: JD Daley
board.case: Jefferson, Josh Allen, and Rice kept in the 7th. Boom-or-bust just built the boom version.

board.name: Collin Krum
board.case: Bijan stays, London and Judkins came with him. Still one piece from the ring after last year's title-game trip.

board.name: Vincent Cannarozzi
board.case: JSN and Jeanty up top. The Nabers era is over; this is the rebuild that has to hit.

board.name: Jared Hall
board.case: Taylor and Nabers are the spine. Three rings say don't bury him after a 7-7 reset.

board.name: German Haro
board.case: Cook and Henry in the first two rounds. First time in years the roster isn't a two-win sentence.

board.name: Kyle Fowler
board.case: AJ Brown, DeVonta, and Skattebo kept in the 8th. Young and thin, but not 3-11 thin.
